node-1.label: A 72-year-old woman experienced behavioural changes, unsteadiness, and frequent falls over the past year

node-2.label: Over the past year, relatives reported that she became listless, neglected work and domestic activities, exhibited hyperreligious behaviour, anxiety, loss of appetite, mild lower limb weakness, and falls; later she had episodes of agitation, confusion, and visual hallucinations, leading to initiation of antipsychotic medication, and eventually lost the ability to walk and became wheelchair-bound

node-3.label: On admission, she showed disorientation, apathy, apraxia, short-term memory deficit (MMSE = 7), anosmia, mild flaccid proximal paraparesis, and muscular atrophy; patellar reflexes and plantar responses were normal; urinary incontinence was present without signs of sensory impairment

node-4.label: She had started oral anticoagulant therapy two years earlier due to paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; 24-hour Holter monitoring revealed no paroxysmal atrial fibrillation

node-5.label: A comprehensive workup including vitamin levels, thyroid function, tumour markers, full-body CT, and breast ultrasound was unremarkable; EEG indicated diffuse cerebral dysfunction without epileptic activity

attrs.why: New expert analyses report CSF xanthochromia with 4500 RBC/μL and protein 61, MRI T2* hypointensities extending to frontotemporal, insular, brainstem and spinal regions, and angioMRI showing no bleeding source. The radiologist and laboratory physician conclude this better supports chronic SAH with superficial siderosis and refutes pure FTD, with frontotemporal features possibly secondary. Therefore the neurodegenerative FTD umbrella is no longer the leading explanation, though it cannot be fully excluded without FDG-PET/CSF biomarkers. Confidence decreases from 0.55 to 0.2.

Expert laboratory analysis and prior Holter/anticoagulation indicate vascular etiologies are basically excluded. The MRI T2* signal could suggest vascular factors but is nonspecific and not sufficient to support active vascular cognitive impairment. Confidence decreases from 0.2 to 0.1.

The radiologist reiterates that normal pressure hydrocephalus remains a treatable differential that is not yet excluded, since the current MRI still does not provide Evans index/DESH. Confidence is maintained at 0.2.
Expert analyses and the comprehensive negative systemic workup effectively exclude metabolic/toxic encephalopathy. Confidence decreases from 0.05 to 0.02.

node-10.label: Brain MRI shows cortical and brainstem T2* hypointensities suggesting iron deposition (possible superficial siderosis or vascular factors)

node-11.label: Current MRI does not demonstrate frontotemporal atrophy or Evans index/DESH; FDG-PET and CSF biomarkers are not yet available

attrs.why: New expert analyses describe CSF xanthochromia with 4500 RBC/μL, elevated protein 61, and MRI T2* iron deposition involving cortical, brainstem and spinal regions with arachnoiditis. Both the radiologist and laboratory physician conclude this confirms superficial siderosis from chronic SAH. With this direct supporting evidence and a plausible anticoagulation-related chronic bleeding mechanism, confidence rises from 0.2 to 0.8.

node-16.label: Brain MRI T2* hypointensities involve bilateral frontotemporal, insular, brainstem and spinal regions (radiologist characterization)

node-18.label: CSF examination shows xanthochromia with 4500 RBC/μL and protein 61

node-19.label: AngioMRI reveals no identifiable bleeding source

node-20.label: MRI/CSF evaluation shows spinal thecal iron deposition and arachnoiditis
